script.text: Washington reportedly approved a draft deal with Iran. Why is Hormuz still shut?

Sources told Reuters the U.S. approved a draft memorandum that Qatari mediators presented to Iran. It is the latest attempt to end the war. Qatar says both sides are reviewing proposals. A senior Iranian official says the two sides remain far from a deal.

Iran's security council chief, Mohsen Rezaei, calls the U.S. reply unconvincing. He says Hormuz reopens only if Washington meets seven Iranian conditions, including lifting sanctions and ending the U.S. naval blockade. Iran had offered to reopen the strait within two days on those terms.

Meanwhile, Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers hit mines and caught fire in the strait. That is unverified. Trump confirmed a U.S. strike on an Iranian anti-aircraft site, and says the war ends very soon, one way or the other.
Will Hormuz reopen before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran: US Approves Draft Deal, Hormuz Stays Shut? #shorts
upload.description:
Sources told Reuters that the United States approved a draft memorandum of understanding that Qatari mediators presented to Iran. Qatar says both the U.S. and Iran are reviewing proposals put forward by mediators, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides remain far from a deal. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called the U.S. reply unconvincing and said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if Washington meets Iran's seven conditions, which reportedly include lifting sanctions and ending the U.S. naval blockade. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say several tankers struck mines and caught fire in the strait; this could not be independently verified. President Trump confirmed U.S. forces attacked an Iranian anti-aircraft installation near the strait and said the war would end very soon, one way or the other. Details come from officials and the parties involved; dates and tanker counts differ between outlets.
